acetate@2/openbabel: Open Babel only transforms neutral acids and bases; it never protonates an input carboxylate. Acetic acid pKa 4.76, so pH 2 is the neutral acid.
betaine@2/openbabel: Same Open Babel limitation for the input carboxylate; Burette uses the generic carboxylic acid pKa 4.76 (betaine's own pKa 1.8 is not modelled, see limits).
aniline@2/openbabel: Open Babel's model has no aniline rule. Aniline pKa 4.60 (Perrin 1965), so pH 2 gives the anilinium ion; Dimorphite-DL agrees.
sulfanilamide@2/openbabel: Open Babel has no aniline rule; Burette and Dimorphite-DL protonate the aryl NH2 at pH 2 (generic aniline pKa 4.60).
pyridine@2/openbabel: Open Babel's model has no pyridine rule. Pyridine pKa 5.23 (Perrin 1965), so pH 2 gives pyridinium; Dimorphite-DL agrees.
ciprofloxacin@2/openbabel: Independent sites: Burette and Dimorphite-DL also protonate the N-aryl piperazine N (generic aniline pKa 4.60). The coupled real value is far lower, so Open Babel's monocation is the better answer here; coupling is a documented limit.
metformin@2/openbabel: Open Babel protonates both biguanide imines. Burette treats the imine bridging two amidine carbons as non-basic, giving the monocation (pKa1 about 12.4; Dimorphite-DL agrees). The second protonation (pKa2 about 2.8) is a documented limit.
metformin@7.4/openbabel: Open Babel's dication is not the physiological form; metformin is a monocation at pH 7.4 (pKa2 about 2.8).
metformin@12/openbabel: Open Babel's dication; Burette keeps the guanidine-type monocation (pKa1 about 12.4, Burette's guanidine row 13.6).
phenol@12/openbabel: Open Babel 3.1.1 does not deprotonate phenol at pH 12. Phenol pKa 9.99 (CRC), so pH 12 gives phenolate; Dimorphite-DL agrees.
paracetamol@12/openbabel: Open Babel does not deprotonate the phenol; paracetamol pKa 9.5 is below 12.
paracetamol@7.4/dimorphite: Dimorphite-DL's phenol estimate deprotonates paracetamol at pH 7.4; its measured pKa is 9.5 (phenol row 9.99), so it is neutral.
ethanethiol@12/openbabel: Open Babel has no thiol rule. Ethanethiol pKa 10.61 (CRC); Dimorphite-DL agrees on the thiolate.
thiophenol@7.4/openbabel: Open Babel has no thiol rule. Thiophenol pKa 6.62 (CRC), so pH 7.4 gives thiophenolate; Dimorphite-DL agrees.
thiophenol@12/openbabel: Open Babel has no thiol rule; thiophenolate at pH 12.
phosphoric acid@7.4/openbabel: Open Babel 3.1.1 leaves free phosphoric acid neutral. pKa 2.16/7.21/12.32 (CRC) gives HPO4(2-) at pH 7.4; Dimorphite-DL agrees.
phosphoric acid@12/openbabel: Open Babel leaves phosphoric acid neutral; HPO4(2-) at pH 12 (pKa3 12.32).
methyl phosphate@2/openbabel: Methyl phosphate pKa1 1.54 (Kumler and Eiler 1943) is below 2, so the monoanion dominates; both references keep the neutral acid.
methyl phosphate@2/dimorphite: Same as Open Babel: Dimorphite-DL's phosphate pKa1 estimate is above 2; Burette follows the measured 1.54.
dimethyl phosphate@2/openbabel: Dimethyl phosphate pKa 1.29 (Kumler and Eiler 1943) is below 2; both references keep the neutral diester acid.
dimethyl phosphate@2/dimorphite: Same as Open Babel; Burette follows the measured pKa 1.29.
methylphosphonic acid@2/dimorphite: Dimorphite-DL's estimate puts pKa1 below 2; the measured pKa1 is 2.38 (Crofts and Kosolapoff 1953), so the neutral acid dominates at pH 2.
methylphosphonic acid@7.4/openbabel: Open Babel has no phosphonic acid rule. The measured pKa1/pKa2 2.38/7.74 give the monoanion at pH 7.4.
methylphosphonic acid@7.4/dimorphite: Dimorphite-DL's pKa2 estimate is below 7.4; Burette uses the measured 7.74, so the monoanion. This site is close to pH 7.4 and either reading is within measurement spread.
methylphosphonic acid@12/openbabel: Open Babel has no phosphonic acid rule; the dianion at pH 12.
dimethylphosphinic acid@7.4/openbabel: Open Babel has no phosphinic acid rule. Measured pKa 3.08 (Crofts and Kosolapoff 1953); Dimorphite-DL agrees on the anion.
dimethylphosphinic acid@12/openbabel: Open Babel has no phosphinic acid rule; the anion at pH 12.
methanesulfonic acid@2/openbabel: Open Babel 3.1.1 leaves sulfonic acids neutral. Methanesulfonic acid pKa -1.9 (Guthrie 1978); Dimorphite-DL agrees on the anion.
methanesulfonic acid@7.4/openbabel: Open Babel leaves sulfonic acids neutral; anion at any pH in 0-14.
methanesulfonic acid@12/openbabel: Open Babel leaves sulfonic acids neutral; anion at any pH in 0-14.
5-methyltetrazole@7.4/openbabel: Open Babel adds the negative charge on another ring N but keeps the N-H, an over-hydrogenated anion. Burette and Dimorphite-DL remove the N-H proton (tetrazole pKa 4.90).
5-methyltetrazole@12/openbabel: Same Open Babel tetrazole quirk as at pH 7.4.
sulfanilamide@12/dimorphite: Burette has no sulfonamide rule (documented limit); Dimorphite-DL deprotonates the primary sulfonamide (pKa about 10.4).
